title: Reverse Each Word

concept.title: Apply an operation to every word
body: Once a line is split into words, you can treat each word on its own: change it, and put the pieces back together in the same order. Reversing a word is a slice with a negative step in Python (`w[::-1]`), `reverse` in C++ and `new StringBuilder(w).reverse()` in Java.

body.code:
words = line.split()
result = " ".join(w[::-1] for w in words)

body: Do not confuse this with reversing the order of the words: here the words stay in their places and only their letters change direction.

statement: Given a line of text, reverse the letters of every word but keep the words in their original order. Print the words separated by single spaces.
inputFormat: A single line of text with at least one word. Words are separated by one or more spaces.
outputFormat: Print the line with every word reversed.
constraints: The line has between 1 and 1000 characters.
hints: Reverse each word on its own.
Join the reversed words with single spaces, in the original order.

explanation: Split into words, reverse each word separately and join them again in the same order.

code.python:
s = input()

words = s.split()
print(" ".join(w[::-1] for w in words))
